chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr, who said:

I asked him about one who forgets the second sajdah of the second rakʿah, or doubts concerning it. So he said: If you fear that you only placed your face down once, then when you give salām, perform one sajdah and place your face down once, and there is no sahw upon you.

So this does not contradict the detail that we presented earlier, because his statement, 'the one who forgets the second sajdah of the second rakʿah,' may mean that he intended the second rakʿah of the last two rakʿahs. In the apparent wording of the report, it is not specified whether it is the second rakʿah of the first two or of the last two; rather, it can bear both meanings together. So when that is possible, we interpret it as the second rakʿah of the last two, so that it accords with what was detailed in the first report.

key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the transmitted report or hadith narration
key_terms.سَلَّمْتَ: you concluded the prayer with salām
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: forgetfulness requiring remedial consideration in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forget the second sajdah of the second rakʿah in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for one who forgets or doubts the second sajdah in prayer and indicates that a missed sajdah may be made up after salat. The compiler then reconciles the report with earlier narrations by interpreting it as referring to the second rakʿah of the final two rakʿahs, preserving consistency in legal detail.
